post:

headline: Superman: The Stranger Logo Dark Origin Revealed
post:
Hey friends! According to Screen Rant, a brand new comic panel reveals a surprisingly dark origin for the hero's iconic emblem. In the upcoming Superman: The Stranger #3, the legendary symbol appears to come from a tragic workplace fire at the Saturn Building where Clark once worked before his powers fully developed. 

Instead of alien origins or a family design, this version of the emblem reportedly stands for "Saturn" to serve as a reminder of a devastating blaze that claimed the lives of everyone trapped inside while he survived. Clark is apparently carrying that heavy guilt with him as he starts his journey to protect Metropolis.

Issue #3 arrives this Wednesday, November 4, 2026, bringing plenty of new context for this heartbreaking piece of lore. What do you think about this surprising new twist for the Man of Steel? 🦸‍♂️🔥

#Superman #DCComics #ScreenRant
original_title: In Just 1 Panel, Superman's New Logo Changes Everything About His Lore With New Release

headline: You Can See Everything beats Clayface
post:
The box office has a brand new king for the Halloween weekend! Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary You Can See Everything took the No. 1 spot with $11.4 million, pushing the DC body-horror villain movie Clayface down to No. 2 with $11 million in its second weekend.

Clayface has now earned $83 million against its estimated $40 million plus budget, while the documentary sits at $64.7 million. 

Which of these two theatrical releases did you like the best?

#BoxOffice #Clayface #Documentary
original_title: Clayface Just Lost the Box Office to 2026’s Biggest Surprise Hit & It’s A Game-Changing Moment For Movies

headline: DC Celebrates Green Lantern Lore
post:
Hey superhero fans! DC recently released a stunning collection of character art, according to Screen Rant. These pieces highlight the stars of the multi-colored Corps. Back in 2005, the Rebirth era brought us the Emotional Spectrum. This massive power source is made up of different emotions and colors.

Jorge Fornés created an incredible series of variant covers for Green Lantern Corps issues 15 through 21. Each image shows a Lantern in a characteristic pose alongside their specific emotion. This artwork essentially combines into a gigantic art piece celebrating the franchise's breakout modern characters.

Several of these figures have even led their own spin-off titles over the years. It is a wonderful tribute to the expansive mythos of the cosmic heroes. 🟢

Which color from the Emotional Spectrum is your absolute favorite?

#GreenLantern #DCComics #ComicBooks
original_title: DC Celebrates Green Lantern Lore With Peak Art Of Each Different Color
